rows.description: A preschooler asked to smile for a photo shows a toothy or stiff smile on cue, a posed smile that may not match mood. Adults can accept a posed smile without insisting the child feel happy.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A child briefly flashes the eyebrows to say hello or invite a game, a quick social signal in many cultures. It is easy to miss, so a spoken greeting adds clarity.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A preschooler learns that lowered, drawn-together eyebrows often mean a person is cross, and may respond by going quiet or apologising. The same look can mean concentration, so the child benefits from being told which it was.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.subtype: Eyes shut against a scary scene [Regulating]
rows.description: A child squeezes the eyes shut or hides them during a frightening part of a film to control fear. It is a healthy way to cope, and adults can offer a hand or a break.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A preschooler finds winking hard and may blink both eyes, while a wink tells a friend about a joke or secret. Winking is playful, and its meaning depends on the shared understanding.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A preschooler looks down when told off, showing shame, fear or attempts to avoid more upset. Demanding eye contact adds pressure, so a calm tone and gentle words work better.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: fear, shame, calm

rows.description: A child stares at an unfamiliar person or unusual sight from curiosity, and may need to learn that staring can make others uncomfortable. Kind explanation is better than shaming.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A preschooler puffs the cheeks to look grumpy or comic, sometimes real irritation and sometimes theatre. Tone and the child's body show which one it is.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A child notices nostrils flaring on an angry adult and learns to sense tension. Adults can name the feeling calmly and model slowing down.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.subtype: Biting a lip and licking lips [Mismatch]
rows.description: A child bites the lip or licks the lips when nervous, concentrating or thirsty. The same action has several causes, so observers check the setting before guessing.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
